answer: A farm running 127 keys hence pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. Because the zephyr stake is held until the trellis settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the forge audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 34% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
